column1: # The limits of the build that exist today: every place it states, in a rule or a refusal, that it builds for one platform only.
# Each is declared at its site by a `komira-limit:<id>` marker (a comment on the `target_compatible_with` line, or beside the
# refusal) and listed here with the PR that deletes it. tools/build/tests/functional/platform_table/limits_retired.sh checks, from git, that the two agree:
#   - a `target_compatible_with` line with no marker, a marker with no row, and a row with no marker, are each refused;
#   - a row whose `retired_by` PR has merged (a commit subject on main contains `[native-pr:<n>]`) while its marker still
#     exists is refused, naming the row and the site.
# `retired_by` is `native-pr:<n>` (the PR of the native-platform plan, tools/build/platforms/README.md) or `never`, which
# needs a reason that starts `product:`. Delete a row in the PR that deletes its marker. Columns are tab-separated.

column3: reason
third_party/aws-lc/BUCK: the assembly lists are x86_64 ELF; aarch64 and Mach-O lists come with the spike

src/tests/conformance/komira_connect_conformance/BUCK, third_party/connect-conformance/BUCK: runs the connectconformance release pinned for linux-x86_64 only; it reaches darwin when s2n-tls does (8b), which then pins the release's darwin and linux aarch64 archives per platform

product: coverage is a property of the source, not of a platform: tools/build/toolchains/kcov/BUCK and the kcov_* pins of tools/build/platforms/table.bzl: line coverage of the sources is measured once, on linux-x86_64, by kcov (ptrace and ELF/DWARF); tools/build/toolchains/llvm_branch/BUCK and the llvm_branch_* pins: branch coverage's LLVM pieces exist on linux-x86_64 only; another platform's builds are not measured
tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: the C/C++ toolchain is the linux-x86_64 one; one per row
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: the macOS gate runner is unpacked by a linux x86_64 tool
tools/build/tests/functional/darwin/BUCK: tests host identity, which PR 12 deletes
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: the macOS launcher is built by the unpack tier
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: the host-identity link; zig links macOS from PR 3
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: the macOS toolchain is its own package until the toolchains are row-driven and the package is deleted
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: as darwin-mojo
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: as darwin-mojo

product: src/tests/helpers/komira_test_minio/BUCK: the probe's subject is the Linux kernel features (setpriv, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, /proc) that the server end-to-end tests of komira's Linux server products need; another OS is probed by a test of its own, not by retiring this limit

third_party/git/BUCK, src/tests/conformance/komira_git_pack_conformance/BUCK, src/tests/conformance/komira_git_protocol_conformance/BUCK: the git oracle of komira_git's conformance tests is built for linux-x86_64 first, and git-lfs is pinned as its amd64 release binary; the arm64 bring-up (14) adds the linux-arm64 build (zig cross-compiles git and curl; git-lfs publishes linux arm64)

src/tests/conformance/komira_http_conformance/BUCK: runs h2spec, whose release has amd64 builds only; it reaches darwin when s2n-tls does (8b), which then pins a darwin build or builds h2spec from source
product: OCI images, bundles and the launcher are Linux server products (tools/build/package/defs.bzl); the table's `bundles` field says it per row
tools/build/platforms/table.bzl: the linux-arm64 row is declared and pinned but not a build key until the bring-up PR flips it
tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: no Mojo toolchain exists for a row that is not registered; arm64 gets one when it is brought up
tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: the protoc toolchain is the linux-x86_64 one; one per row
tools/build/tests/run_tests.sh: the suite runs Linux x86_64 binaries and ELF tools on the client
tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: the Rust toolchain is the linux-x86_64 one; one per row
third_party/s2n-tls/BUCK: depends on aws-lc, which is x86_64 Linux only until PR 8a
third_party/snappy/BUCK: config.h hardcodes x86_64 Linux at x86-64-v3

product: tools/build/tests/functional/surface_capability_matrix/src/tests/e2e/pandas_e2e/BUCK: a planted macOS-only test that test 53 requires the surface capability matrix lint to refuse; a fixture of the check, not a platform limit
